text:
sasha: noticing a weird p95 latency spike on dedicated-gpu-pool-3 starting ~10:12 UTC. grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/xyz - p95 jumped from 120ms -> 980ms, throughput dropped ~40%. tagging @ajay @lina to triage.

ajay: looking now. any recent deploys to that pool?

sasha: no deploys in the last 6h. autoscaler also didn't change replica counts. logs show a lot of streaming backpressure errors and repeated requeues. snippet: `rpc: stream write blocked for >200ms`

lina: I pulled profiler from the affected node. kernel-selection churn shows fallback from small-seq kernels to generic matmul at request time for many calls. suspect sequence-length spikes. attaching mini dump.

ajay: can you paste the kernel profiler top lines?

lina: sure: ```
# kernel selection log (excerpt)
2024-06-27T10:12:05Z SELECT kernel=attn_opt_small seq=64 cost=12.3
2024-06-27T10:12:06Z SELECT kernel=matmul_fallback seq=512 cost=9.8
2024-06-27T10:12:06Z RESHARD -> fallback due to kv_cache_miss
2024-06-27T10:12:07Z SELECT kernel=matmul_fallback seq=1024 cost=14.1
```

sasha: interesting — kv_cache_miss entries spike correlated with the latency burst. maybe KV cache eviction thrash causing recomputation and huge seqs?

ajay: I also see one pod in the pool with >90% PCIe bandwidth and >70% host memory usage. noisy neighbor candidate. bench-bot traces show heavy streaming sessions from a single client id.

perf-bot: anomaly alert: client_id=cli-42 submitted 120 requests in 30s with median prompt tokens=900, many with tool-call loops (function-calls) and streaming enabled. repeated append patterns detected.

sasha: that matches. long prompts + streaming = huge KV cache growth per request. our batching heuristic collapsed because it assumed seq distribution < 256. Suddenly many seqs at 900-1k forced fallback kernels and long runtimes.

lina: also saw a burst of cache GC activity: eviction thrash logs: `kv_cache.size rapidly changing 1.2GB -> 200MB -> 1.1GB` which caused memory reclaim and kernel context switches.

ajay: root cause hypothesis: misbehaving client (tool-calling loop) produced unexpectedly long token sequences + perpetual streaming -> per-request KV cache blowup and batching heuristic picked high-latency kernel leading to head-of-line blocking and throughput collapse. noisy neighbor amplified PCIe contention.

sasha: mitigation plan (short term): 1) throttle streaming rate and max prompt tokens for that client id, 2) evict the noisy pod from dedicated-gpu-pool-3, 3) add a temporary routing policy to steer new requests to pool-1.

lina: I've issued a throttle on client_id=cli-42 and limited max_tokens=256 for streaming sessions. also quarantined the pod (cordon + drain).

ajay: rolling routing policy applied: routing.rule.client_profile=steer->pool-1. monitoring.

perf-bot: alert muted for this thread. p95 dropped to ~160ms within 90s after actions. throughput recovered to ~85% baseline.

sasha: nice. next actions (post-incident): 1) improve batching heuristic to detect heavy tail seq distribution and avoid optimistic small-kernel choices when KV growth observed, 2) add fast path to cap effective KV cache window per-streaming-session to avoid O(seq^2) growth from tool-call loops, 3) add telemetry to record per-request predicted vs actual seq and kernel switch counts, 4) update autoscaler to detect PCIe saturation signals.

ajay: I'll own the autoscaler PCIe saturation signal work. will propose metrics by EOD.

lina: I'll prototype a per-session KV window cap and a safety check in kernel selector to prefer stable kernels when cache churn > threshold.

sasha: i'll write an incident blameless postmortem and coordinate an RFC for the batching heuristic change.

bench-bot: load replay ready for testing. I can replay the offending client's trace at reduced rate to validate changes.

sasha: thanks. assign follow-ups: ajay (autoscaler metrics), lina (kv cap + kernel selector), sasha (postmortem + RFC), bench-bot (replay). marking resolved for now but will keep monitoring for 24h. :white_check_mark:

ajay: noted. I'll also add a short-term scheduling guard: avoid colocating >2 heavy-streaming sessions on same host. low-effort stopgap.

lina: adding unit tests for kernel selector to ensure it doesn't flip kernels more than twice per request under noisy signals.

sasha: closing thread for now. if the p95 creeps back up ping this thread. thanks everyone :rocket:
